name: E. coli chemotaxis: receptor methylation driven by a held log-ligand input
question: Which functions of the history of the attractant concentration do the kinase activity and the methylation level represent?

provenance.source: Tu, Shimizu and Berg, PNAS 105, 14855 (2008), doi:10.1073/pnas.0807569105: a = G(m, [L]) (Eqs. 2-4), f_m = alpha (m0 - m), dm/dt = F(a) piecewise linear (Fig. 2 legend); values from the text after Fig. 1 and the Fig. 2 legend

assumptions: mean field; ligand binding and kinase activity at quasi-equilibrium (as in the source)
K_A = K_I/C with C = 0.0062 (the source states C, not K_A)
time in units of 1/F(0) (F(0) = 1 in the source's simulations; physical F(0) about 7e-3 per s)
F(a) written as a line plus abs terms; identical to the source's piecewise-linear form
the input u = ln([L]/[L]0) with [L]0 = 158 uM, the geometric mean of the source's 50-500 uM range (Fig. 3); amplitude 1.151, the source's A_L = (1/2) ln([L]_h/[L]_l)
u redrawn for every interval of 0.05/F(0) and held within it (the source uses ramps, sine waves and a pulse)

observables: 1/(1 + exp(Nc*(alpha*(m0 - m) + log(1 + L0*exp(u)/KI) - log(1 + L0*exp(u)/KA))))
